copied_from.why: PLAN.md §1: values are copied, not linked. A duplicated table is cheaper than a coupling to harness-core, which is untouched evidence for the experiments. The cost of copying is drift, and this block is the only defence — it names the upstream revision these rates came from so a mismatch is discoverable.
copied_from.drift_check: diff these rates against harness-core/config/routing.json's model_prices_usd_per_mtok. A difference means one of the two is stale; neither file's version stamp alone can tell you which.

columns.cache_write: cache write at the 5-minute TTL, 1.25x input. The default and the overwhelmingly common case: this session's gateway applies a 5m TTL unless a request explicitly asks otherwise.
columns.cache_write_1h: cache write at the 1-hour TTL, 2x input. CHARGED whenever a record's own counts report a 1h portion. The first version of this file called the column unreachable and declined to charge it; that was measured false on 2026-07-30. With the anthropic-beta extended-cache-ttl-2025-04-11 header, a sonnet-5 request carrying cache_control ttl 1h returned ephemeral_1h_input_tokens 25204 against this gateway. The narrower statement, and the limit of what was actually observed: the gateway HONOURS an explicit 1h breakpoint on a direct API call. That does not establish that Claude Code's own requests ever set one, and prior evidence in this project was that its breakpoints get rejected — so 5m stays the default and this column is reached only by a record that reports a 1h count. Pricing a 1h portion at the 5m rate understates it by 1.6x.
columns.how_the_two_write_columns_split: MEASURED, not assumed: the flat cache_creation_input_tokens field is the TOTAL ACROSS TTL BUCKETS, not the 5-minute portion. The same response reporting 25204 flat also reported ephemeral_5m_input_tokens 0 and ephemeral_1h_input_tokens 25204. So charging the flat field at the 5m rate and then adding the 1h column bills the same tokens twice. lib/prices.mjs derives the 5m portion as total minus 1h unless the record states an explicit 5m count, and refuses (complete:false) rather than clamping when a 1h portion exceeds the total it belongs to.

billing_assumption: First-party Claude API, standard (non-batch) list rates, inference_geo global (no 1.1x data-residency multiplier), fast mode off. Batch (-50%), fast mode (Opus $10/$50), and US-only residency (1.1x) stack on top and are NOT reflected here.

unpriced_by_design.long_context: Ids carrying a [1m] marker (observed: claude-opus-4-8[1m], anthropic.claude-opus-4-6-v1[1m]) are the 1M-context variants. Their rates are above the standard row past 200k and are not published here, so they are reported as unpriced rather than charged at the standard rate. A premium call billed at the standard rate is a plausible figure that is quietly too low, which is worse than a hole.

claude-sonnet-5.policy: DECIDED BY THE USER 2026-07-30: the model row below carries the STANDARD $3/$15, and the introductory rate above is recorded but NOT applied. Two reasons, both comparability: every Alfred figure stays directly comparable to Experiment 2 arm B's recorded $18.483, which was measured on sonnet-4-6 at $3/$15; and no figure changes meaning when the step-up arrives on 2026-09-01. Cost of the choice, stated so nobody later 'fixes' it back: until 2026-09-01 every reported dollar figure runs 1.5x ABOVE what was actually billed. That is a deliberate conservative bias — an estimate that overstates is safe, one that flatters is not — and it is the opposite of this table's governing failure mode, where an unpriced model made a run look cheap.
claude-sonnet-5.why_recorded_at_all: A rate we decline to charge is still a fact about the world. Dropping it would make this decision indistinguishable from never having noticed the step-up — the difference between a choice and an oversight.

free_by_design.<synthetic>: Not a billable model. It is the recorded model value for assistant entries that carry no model id, and it exists so those entries stop forcing cost.complete:false. It is the one id for which $0 is the honest figure, so it must not be reported as unpriced.
